section_summary.extract_value: This Introduction reviews literature linking negative and positive body image (body appreciation) to women's sexual health and frames BMI as an important factor potentially altering those relationships. The authors state the paper's purpose is to examine relationships between body appreciation and sexual function across body sizes and list three explicit hypotheses testing BMI effects, body appreciation effects, and BMI as a moderator of the body appreciation–sexual function relationship.
section_summary.evidence_source: The purpose of this study was to explore relationships between body appreciation and sexual function in women of various body sizes and to assess whether a measure of body size such as BMI alters this relationship. We tested three hypotheses: Hypothesis 1 was that BMI would predict overall sexual function and specific components of sexual function. Hypothesis 2 was that body appreciation would predict overall sexual function and specific components of sexual function. Hypothesis 3 was that BMI would moderate the relationship between body appreciation and sexual function.
